title: Meeting Rooms II
description: Given a list of meeting `Interval` objects, return the minimum number of conference rooms needed so that every meeting gets a room. Overlapping meetings need separate rooms; a meeting ending at time `t` and another starting at `t` may share a room.
hints: The answer is the largest number of meetings happening at the same moment.
Consider the start times and end times as two separately sorted lists.
Sweep the starts; each time a start occurs before the earliest unfinished end, you need a new room, otherwise a room frees up and you advance the end pointer.

solution.explanation: The number of rooms equals the maximum overlap. Sort start times and end times separately and use two pointers: for each start, if it is before the earliest unmatched end, a new room is needed (count grows); otherwise a meeting has finished and its room is reused (end pointer advances). Track the maximum count. Sorting gives O(n log n) time and O(n) space; a min-heap of end times works equally well.
